anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level SQL or transaction design obliges the database engine to touch more data, rows, or time than the true business requirement demands.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Optimizer metadata is stale, incomplete, or inaccurate, provoking systematic cardinality misestimates and sub-optimal plan selection.

When both root causes coexist, the database exhibits severe and erratic performance degradation: statements already scanning or joining excessive data are paired with execution plans that underestimate or overestimate row counts, leading the optimizer to choose nested-loop scans where hash joins are needed (or vice-versa), to allocate wrong memory grants, and to spill to disk. Slow-query logs show the same statements with wildly different runtimes, blocking chains lengthen as mis-estimated queries hold locks longer, and resource monitors report oscillating CPU spikes, temp-space surges, and bursty I/O. Autonomic tuning and statistics refresh operations may thrash, causing frequent recompilations without relief, while application tiers experience cascading timeouts, retries, and throughput collapse.

Causally, inefficient SQL shapes created by the application magnify the impact of bad statistics: wide scans, non-sargable predicates, and bulky IN lists increase the sensitivity of plan quality to accurate cardinality estimates. Conversely, stale or missing statistics deprive the optimizer of the information it needs to mitigate poor SQL patterns, so it selects plans that further inflate data access, memory use, and lock duration. The feedback loop—sub-optimal SQL inflating row counts, statistics misestimation hiding the real cost, and the resulting plans compounding both—drives the database into progressively worse performance and stability states.

entry.official_description: The total number of locks exceeds the lock table size
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with concurrent transactions contending for the same logical resources, incompatible lock acquisition order, or transaction-state conflicts surfaced by the engine.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking chains, reduce conflicting write overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, review lock acquisition order, and verify whether transaction scheduling or retry logic needs adjustment.
